Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-02-27 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 54 minutes
- Attendees: Jasmine Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Elaine Wu (Procurement), Derek Price (Security), Ravi Menon (VP Eng), Sophie Laurent (Legal), Tommy Ng (Finance)

Auto-summary:
Redwood and StrataScale reviewed the legal intake playbook focusing on aligning MSA and DPA language with StrataScale's platform operations constraints. Key topics: data residency, audit logs, SLA definitions (uptime vs latency SLO), exceptions, pricing approval pathways (pilot pricing vs committed reserved), and next steps for redlines and a technical pilot. Action owners and deadlines captured.

Topics:
- MSA redlines and exception triage
- DPA's data residency & retention specifics
- SLA metrics and remediation credits vs termination rights
- Pricing pathways: pilot, reserved/dedicated, private deployment costs
- Security artifacts: SOC 2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, RBAC
- Technical pilot scope and timeline

[00:00] Jasmine (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We want to make this an intake-style session — get the legal asks, procurement timeline and make sure SEs have what they need to scope the pilot. Elaine, do you want to start with timeline?

[00:25] Elaine (Procurement): Yeah hi thanks. We're under a quarterly procurement window so ideally terms signed by mid-April. We have the usual DPA requirements and a couple of internal redlines — data residency for EU workloads, and limited log retention for PII. We'll also need pricing approval to go through finance — Tommy will lead that.

[01:10] Tommy (Finance): Right, timeline is aggressive but feasible. We'll need clear committed vs overage pricing tiers and a simple comparison: pay-as-you-go hosted vs reserved dedicated. Also any one-time setup or onboarding fees.

[02:05] Ravi (VP Eng): From an engineering perspective, we want to validate latency and stability before committing. If we do dedicated/reserved we need an autoscale guarantee for bursts, or fallback to hosted. We also want to know KV cache behavior — sorry KV cash — how the token cache is handled and if that affects multi-tenant performance.

[07:30] Marco (SE): Quick clarifier: our runtime separates KV cache per customer on Dedicated and we can route requests with policy — e.g., latency-priority to dedicated, cost-priority to hosted. For private deployments (VPC/on-prem) key material stays in customer KMS if desired. I can share an architecture diagram.

[12:15] Sophie (Legal): On the MSA side we have two sticky items: indemnity language for model outputs and the SLA termination triggers. We prefer remediation credits over termination for first-tier incidents, and explicit definitions for "downtime" vs "performance degradation". Also need to confirm retention for logs used in audits — minimum 90 days but not more than 12 months unless otherwise agreed.

[18:00] Jasmine (AE): Helpful. Our standard MSA includes a service-level agreement with availability targets and credit formulas. We also offer an enterprise appendix for Dedicated/Private with specific commitments. Where would Sophie like to see an initial compromise?

[25:05] Sophie (Legal): Send a redline that narrows the termination rights and adds a 30-day remediation period with staged credits. For data retention — we want an option to cap logs for EU customers to 90 days; global logs can be 12 months but only if explicit consent. We'll send our DPA template later today.

[32:10] Derek (Security): Security check — we need to confirm encryption at rest + in transit, customer-managed KMS support, and key rotation. Also, audit logging must include token-level traces for forensic needs, but we prefer pseudonymization in exported logs. Is that supported?

[40:00] Marco (SE): On encryption: yes, we support customer KMS/HSM integrations for Private deployments and can offer envelope encryption for hosted/dedicated. For token-level traces, we can redact sensitive fields and provide structured logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders. There's a tradeoff with storage/retention that we'll highlight in the security pack.

[47:20] Elaine (Procurement): For pricing approval, we need a simple worksheet: 3 scenarios — 1) Hosted paygo (no commit), 2) Dedicated reserved (monthly commit with discount and burst allowance), 3) Private on-prem (one-time infra + licensing). Also list SLA tiers and corresponding credits. Tommy wants break-even points at 3 and 12 months.

[52:30] Jasmine (AE): Great, action items noted. We'll produce a combined packet: MSA redline, DPA alignment note, security artifacts (SOC2 + KMS details), and a pricing worksheet. Marco will prepare the pilot scope to validate latency and KV cache behavior. We'll target sending materials by the first week of March and aim to schedule the technical pilot for week of 2026-03-09.

[53:20] Sophie (Legal): Sounds good. One tiny note — we'll likely require a minor DPA addition for regulatory audits. We'll flag the exact language when we send it.

[53:45] Jasmine (AE): Thanks all. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for the pilot kick-off and track action items in the CRM. Have a good afternoon.
